Published online:

Geographic focus:
United States (Jackson Hole, Wyoming — global central banking context)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical observation YES
T2. Forward-looking immediate YES
T3. Long-term development YES

Synopsis:
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered his Jackson Hole keynote acknowledging inflation remains stubbornly above the 2% target (PCE at 3.7% YoY as of July), signaling a hawkish pivot closer to endorsing rate hikes if incoming data doesn't show clear improvement. Markets repriced September hike probability from ~40% to ~60%. Warsh stopped short of explicit forward guidance but made clear the Fed's "predominant focus" is prices, that financial conditions show "few signs of policy restraint," and that the current 3.50%–3.75% policy rate may need to rise. Three FOMC members had already dissented in favor of tightening at the July meeting. Key August jobs and CPI data due early September will be pivotal for the September 15–16 decision.
